cards.text: Israel's dividing up the land of Canaan, and now we get the allotment for the clans of the tribe of Judah. The south runs from the Salt Sea past Kadesh-barnea to the Brook of Egypt, the east is the Salt Sea, the north climbs right past the Jebusites at Jerusalem, and the west is the Great Sea. That border takes more turns than I did feeling my way around the back of a junk drawer in the dark.
Then Joshua gives a portion among the sons of Judah to Caleb son of Jephunneh. And it's not Joshua's idea. He does it according to the LORD's command.

cards.question: Which city does Joshua give to Caleb?

cards.text: Hebron used to be called Kiriath-arba. And Arba? He was the forefather of Anak, so this city comes with some family history attached.

cards.question: Caleb's new city of Hebron has descendants of Anak in it. What does Caleb do about them?

cards.text: And Caleb is NOT done. From there he marches against Debir, a city once called Kiriath-sepher, and he makes an offer to whoever captures it.

cards.question: Caleb says the man who strikes down Kiriath-sepher and captures it will get his ___ in marriage.
True or false: The man who captures Kiriath-sepher is Caleb's own nephew.

cards.text: So Othniel, son of Caleb's brother Kenaz, takes the city and marries Caleb's daughter Acsah. One day Acsah urges Othniel to ask her father for a field.

cards.question: When Acsah gets off her donkey, Caleb has a question for her. What does he ask?
Acsah tells Caleb he has given her land in the Negev. What does she ask him to give her as well?
How does Caleb answer his daughter Acsah's request?

answers.text: He gives her the upper and lower springs
He gives her a field beside Hebron
He sends her back to ask Joshua

cards.text: Then comes Judah's inheritance city by city, each with its villages, from the Negev and the foothills to the hill country and the wilderness, with Beersheba, Lachish, Hebron and En-gedi on the list. First time I read it out loud, I lost my place twice and had to start all over at Kabzeel.
Now one last line. It's about Jerusalem, and the Jebusites living there.

cards.question: True or false: The descendants of Judah drive the Jebusites out of Jerusalem.
So how do things stand in Jerusalem "to this day"?

answers.text: The city lies empty and in ruins

findings.problem: The setup says the last line is about "the Jebusites living there" in Jerusalem. That tells the baker the Jebusites are still in the city, so it gives away card 15 (Judah did not drive them out) and rules out its wrong answer before the baker picks.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Papa Dorin is only lightly funny. There are just two jokes, both mild: the junk drawer turns on card 1 and losing his place at Kabzeel on card 13. Most story cards are plain retelling, like card 2, card 4 ("some family history attached"), card 6 and card 9, and they read like a nice dad being pleasant. Moments like Caleb's marriage offer, Acsah getting off her donkey and asking for more, or the Jebusites staying put could hold a real laugh without muddying a fact.

rule.text: Not mildly amusing. Laugh-out-loud funny, the kind a baker repeats to a friend. Because he talks naturally, the funny moments come up a lot: in his reactions, his comparisons, his disbelief and his self-deprecation. When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
